anomalies.observed: On the Microcontroller sheet, U10 pin 2 (DIAG_EN) is connected to +12V, while pin 1 (IN) is connected to NET0010.
anomalies.expected: DIAG_EN and IN should both be driven by the ESP32 GPIO1 heater-control net, as specified.

evidence.quote: U10 TPS1H200AQDGNRQ1: pin 2 DIAG_EN connects to +12V; pin 1 IN connects to NET0010 (Microcontroller sheet, page 2).
IN/DIAG_EN (pins 1/2) are both driven from ESP32 GPIO1 on the /Microcontroller/HEATER net.

anomalies.impact: DIAG_EN is no longer controlled by the heater signal. Tying this control input directly to 12 V may exceed its allowed input voltage and damage U10; even if it survives, its diagnostic enable state will not track the intended GPIO control.

parsed.summary: U10's DIAG_EN pin is tied to +12V in the schematic instead of the GPIO1 heater-control net specified for both DIAG_EN and IN. This is a clear control-net deviation and may overvoltage the switch input.
